Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray in Figure 3a displays multiple, bilateral, ill-defined nodular and patchy opacities (often described as acinar or alveolar shadows) rather than solitary lesions, which is characteristic of the diffuse/multifocal form of bronchioloalveolar carcinoma (BAC). This pattern distinguishes it from the localized solitary nodule type and aligns with the description of increased infiltration consistent with diffuse disease.
